reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes precipitation and mechanical properties in a completely different alloy system (VCrFeTaxWx) and does not address grain-boundary precipitation, ductility of precipitates, or caloric response. It provides no support for the key premises about the target (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy.
premises: Thermal annealing can induce in-situ precipitation of a fine, ductile secondary phase along grain boundaries in the target alloy.
Such precipitates will reinforce intergranular cohesion and arrest crack propagation.
The precipitates will have minimal impact on the crystallographic and magnetic/magnetocaloric structure governing the caloric response.
The intervention will yield higher compressive strength and reduced cracking compared to the untreated alloy.
